hook.text: The US spends $4.3 trillion on healthcare. 75% goes to treating chronic diseases that prevention could reduce.

buildup.text: Preventive healthcare companies use wearables, genetic testing, and AI to catch diseases before symptoms appear.

discovery.text: Whoop and Oura ring track sleep, stress, and recovery. Data-driven prevention replaces symptom-based treatment.

twist.text: Insurance companies save money from prevention but rarely pay for it. The incentive system is backward.

climax.text: Preventive healthcare is cheaper and better—but the business model requires fixing misaligned incentives first.

punchline.text: 75% from preventable disease. Prevention is cheaper but nobody pays for it yet.

quiz.question: Why is preventive healthcare underinvested despite being cheaper?
options: Insurance incentives don't align with paying for prevention
